Sealing that protects what it encloses.

Electrical assemblies fail at their seals. Compound and geometry are selected for ingress performance and long-term compression set rather than initial fit alone — a gasket that seals on the bench and relaxes in year three has failed.

Gasket profiles and compounds chosen to hold their sealing force over years of service, not just at first assembly. Compression set measured to ASTM D395 Method B, which we run in-house — it is the number that predicts whether the enclosure still seals in year five.
Silicone from −60 to +220 °C for elevated-temperature enclosures, retaining flexibility across the range. EPDM −40 to +140 °C where the enclosure is weather-exposed rather than hot.
Sealed geometries for enclosures exposed to particulate, moisture and industrial atmospheres. The gasket is one input to your enclosure’s IEC 60529 test; the rating belongs to the assembly.

Isolation mounts and pads that protect sensitive assemblies from mechanical shock. Isolation only begins above about 1.4 times the system natural frequency, so the mount is sized to the mass it carries.

Silicone, −60 to +220 °C, for elevated temperature and the widest service range. Selection is driven by temperature, exposure and the compression set your design allows.
Do you make grommets to non-standard panel thicknesses?

Yes. Grommets are specified by panel hole diameter, panel thickness and groove width, and produced against your drawing. The groove width is your panel thickness — measure the sheet, not the hole — and the bore is set by the cable or conduit passing through.
Is there a minimum order quantity?

Yes — we are a volume manufacturer. Margo produces in bulk against OEM schedules rather than in small lots. Minimum run is 10,000 pieces per part number, per compound, and on larger or more complex parts the minimum is quoted against the part. Prototype and first-article lots sit outside the minimum and are quoted separately, with a prototype within 48 to 72 hours of an approved drawing. Existing tooling ships in three to four weeks ex-works Nashik, or two weeks express where we have confirmed capacity.
Can you match an existing part we currently buy?

Yes. Send a physical sample and we will produce a drawing, confirm compound selection and quote tooling where required. Tell us how the current part fails if it does — whether it hardens, splits or takes a set — because that decides the compound more reliably than the sample does.
